candidates.title: Efficient Multi-Model Orchestration for Self-Hosted Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Self-hosting large language models (LLMs) is increasingly appealing for organizations seeking privacy, cost control, and customization. Yet deploying and maintaining in-house models poses challenges in GPU utilization, workload routing, and reliability. We introduce Pick and Spin, a practical framework that makes self-hosted LLM orchestration scalable and economical. Built on Kubernetes, it integrates a unified Helm-based deployment system, adaptive scale-to-zero automation, and a hybrid routing module that balances cost, latency, and accuracy using both keyword heuristics and a lightweight DistilBERT classifier. We evaluate four models, Llama-3 (90B), Gemma-3 (27B), Qwen-3 (235B), and DeepSeek-R1 (685B) across eight public benchmark datasets, with five inference strategies, and two routing variants encompassing 31,019 prompts and 163,720 inference runs. Pick and Spin achieves up to 21.6% higher success rates, 30% lower latency, and 33% lower GPU cost per query compared with static deployments of the same models.
candidates.reason: Kubernetes上で自己ホストLLMを運用するPick and Spinは、Helmによる統一デプロイ、スケールトゥゼロ自動化、コスト・レイテンシ・精度を両立させるキーワード＋DistilBERT分類器のハイブリッドルーティングを備え、静的デプロイ比でレイテンシ30%減・クエリあたりGPUコスト33%減を実測している。LLMサービング基盤への直接の技術的貢献が確認できる。

candidates.title: HALO: Communication-Aware Heterogeneous 2.5-D System for Energy-Efficient LLM Execution at Edge
candidates.venue: IEEE Journal on Emerging and Selected Topics in Circuits and Systems
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are used to perform various tasks, especially in the domain of natural language processing (NLP). State-of-the-art LLMs consist of a large number of parameters that necessitate a high volume of computations. Currently, GPUs are the preferred choice of hardware platform to execute LLM inference. However, monolithic GPU-based systems executing large LLMs pose significant drawbacks in terms of fabrication cost and energy efficiency. In this work, we propose a heterogeneous 2.5D chiplet-based architecture for accelerating LLM inference. The proposed 2.5D system consists of heterogeneous chiplets connected via a network-on-package (NoP). In the proposed 2.5D system, we leverage the energy efficiency of in-memory computing (IMC) and the general-purpose computing capability of CMOS-based floating point units (FPUs). The 2.5D technology helps to integrate two different technologies (IMC and CMOS) on the same system. Due to a large number of parameters, communication between chiplets becomes a significant performance bottleneck if not optimized while executing LLMs. To this end, we propose a communication-aware scalable technique to map different pieces of computations of an LLM onto different chiplets. The proposed mapping technique minimizes the communication energy and latency over the NoP, and is significantly faster than existing optimization techniques. Thorough experimental evaluations with a wide variety of LLMs show that the proposed 2.5D system provides up to $972\times $ improvement in latency and $1600\times $ improvement in energy consumption with respect to state-of-the-art edge devices equipped with GPU.
candidates.reason: 通信を意識した異種2.5Dチップレット構成でエッジでのLLM実行を高速化するHALOは、最先端GPU搭載エッジデバイス比でレイテンシ最大972倍・エネルギー最大1600倍の改善を評価で示している。対象がLLM推論の実行ハードウェアそのものであり、推論システムへの直接の技術的貢献が確認できる。
